chunk_map.heading: See the loop in your live session
The agent, the harness, the loop

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 (line 1) names 'The agent loop' as the file's own subject, reused at chunk 1 line 3 and chunk 2 line 19/24 — the explicit chunk-0-lede-noun carve-out. Chunk 1 resolves entirely in-chunk: 'that list' (line 15) -> the tool list requested two lines earlier (lines 11/13); 'this session' (lines 11, 13, and inside the line-17 prompt) is the student's own live-session deixis; 'the same set' and 'the list you gave me earlier' (both inside the line-17 prompt) resolve to the tool list Claude itself will have just produced in that same live exchange. Chunk 2 resolves in-chunk: 'that iteration' (line 24) -> 'each iteration' (line 22); 'this same loop' (line 25) -> 'the agent loop' just named (line 24). Harm check: the rule exists to stop a reader from hitting a term with nowhere to anchor it. Closest candidate: raw line 9 ({{prompt:ae101-agent-loop-ascii}}, expands to) 'Name the harness, the LLM, the tool-call step, and how tool results feed back to the LLM' -- 'the harness' is used here two slides before its own definition at line 23. Confirmed via `git diff 1abb84c6..HEAD -- curriculum/lectures/the-agent-loop.md` that the 2026-08-25 reorder moved this prompt ahead of the definitional slide that used to precede it (at the pinned commit, '## The agent, the harness, the loop' was chunk 1 and 'See the loop...' was chunk 2 -- the reverse of today's order). It stays inside because the sentence is an instruction addressed to the student's live Claude Code session, not an assertion the human reader must parse unaided -- the human copy-pastes it and Claude's own answer supplies the term, and the very next slide formalizes it. 'The LLM' and 'the tool-call step' are ordinary compositional engineering vocabulary for this audience, not file-coined terms needing prior naming. Filed as a rule-question in `notes`, not a REVISE, per the dispatch preamble: the harm is marginal (the addressee is the model, not the reader) and the 'fix' of reordering back or rewording away from 'harness' runs against the maintainer's own same-day, explicit 'Do not restore anatomy-first' instruction (line 31).

Scanned both chunks (lines 3-26) for a pointer at another file by position -- none found; the only other-product mentions are named, not located ('Claude Code is one harness; Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI are others.', line 23), naming four products as parallel examples of the defined term rather than a callback to another file's content. `grep -niE 'the opening lecture|the previous module|earlier lecture|earlier module|above|below|further down|at the top of this|see below'` on lines 1-26 -> 0 hits. Closest candidate: line 23's product list -- stays inside because it names things, doesn't locate content by page position, and isn't a callback to a prior slide or file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/predict-before-reveal construction present -- all three prompts are investigate-and-observe (run it, see what comes back), never a guess-first-then-check structure

rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 carries three full live-prompt widgets plus their framing sentences (lines 3-17), each self-carrying. Chunk 2 carries four complete definitional bullets (lines 22-25). Neither chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 1 header 'See the loop in your live session' (line 3) truthfully covers all three prompts: drawing the loop as a diagram, listing its tools, and tracing where the tool list and its injection mechanism come from -- all live introspection of 'the loop' in the student's own session. Chunk 2 header 'The agent, the harness, the loop' (line 19) names exactly the three terms its three defining bullets (lines 22-24) install; the fourth bullet (line 25, long-running sessions) directly extends 'the loop' already in the header rather than contradicting it.

Checked every sub-item across both chunks. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (`grep -E 'Not .*\. Not .*\.'` on lines 1-26 -> 0 hits). No anaphora/epistrophe triple -- line 24's 'Prompt -> reason -> tool calls -> results -> reason again' is a single arrow-chain of distinct concrete stages, not a rhetorical repeat. No self-grading superlative anywhere in the body. No number-with-retraction ('Three prompts' line 5 and 'Four parts' line 22 are plain unretracted counts). No abstraction-noun stack. Closest candidate for the empty-leg verb-triplet check: line 23's 'exposes tool definitions to the LLM, executes the tool calls, and feeds results back in' -- three verbs, but each survives 'what does this concretely mean?' on its own (presents the tool API / runs the call / returns the result), so no leg is empty.

Chunk 1 header 'See the loop in your live session' (line 3) is an orientation/activity header directing the reader into a live-session exercise, functionally the same as the carve-out's 'You are here' / 'The far half opens' examples -- it orients rather than argues. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every bullet/sentence in both chunks against the three low-value classes. Chunk 1: 'Three prompts. Dig into whatever catches you.' (line 5) is a plain scoping instruction, not doctrine restatement or design commentary -- no prior claim is re-announced, and it never tells the student they're inside a pedagogy. Chunk 2's four bullets each add unique defining content (agent / agent harness / agent loop / long-running-session-is-the-same-loop) -- none restates a claim the slide already made, none comments on the curriculum's own design, and no bullet closes with an aphorism restating its own header. No candidate for any of the three classes found in this file.

notes: Rule question for the maintainer (check_slides.md §1, not filed as REVISE): the 2026-08-25 reorder moves the ASCII-diagram prompt ('Name the harness, the LLM, the tool-call step...', raw line 9) ahead of 'agent harness''s own definition (raw line 23) — a genuine forward reference to a file-coined term, confirmed absent at the pinned commit (harness was defined first, prompts ran second, before today's flip). Judged PASS because the text addresses the student's live Claude Code session (copy-paste instruction), not the human reader's own comprehension, and the maintainer's same-day note (line 31) explicitly forbids restoring anatomy-first. But that reorder note attests only that the H1 covers the 'the loop' referent and is silent on 'the harness' — if discovery-before-definition sequencing like this is meant to be a standing pattern, it may be worth a named carve-out in check_slides.md §1 (parallel to the existing session-artifact carve-out) rather than leaving each judge to make the harm call fresh.
